questions.q: Can you tell me about your family?
questions.answer: It's a fairly typical family. There are five of us: my parents, my two sisters and me, although my elder sister is married now and lives in Dhaka with her husband and children. My father ran a small business until he retired recently, and my mother looks after the home. We're quite [[close-knit]], and those of us at home usually have dinner together every night.

questions.q: Do you spend much time with your family?
questions.answer: Quite a lot, especially in the evenings. Once work is done, we tend to gather in the living room over tea and chat about our day. Those relaxed moments help me [[wind down]] after a long day.

questions.q: Who are you closest to in your family?
questions.answer: Probably my younger sister. She's a student and incredibly hard-working, so we often talk about her studies and plans. I feel quite [[protective]] of her, and she's usually the first person I share news with.

questions.q: What do you like to do together as a family?
questions.answer: We love visiting my grandparents in our ancestral village, which isn't far from Sirajganj. The whole family gathers there, especially during Eid, and those visits have an [[unhurried]] warmth that I really treasure.

questions.q: Has your family changed much in recent years?
questions.answer: Quite a bit, actually. My elder sister got married and moved to Dhaka, and my father has recently retired, so he's at home far more. It was a big [[adjustment]] at first, but it's brought us even closer.
